messages:
sam-prod: Quick sync: field backlog is converging on three asks for private deploys: a compact offline bundle for locked-down installs, a "network-handshake" feature to lock external mappings during upgrades, and a clear "maintenance-fastlane" doc for NetOps. Can we scope and owners?

vik-engineering: Agree on splitting into 3 deliverables. Suggest names: `compact-bundle` (bundled artifacts + local verifier), `network-handshake` (pin/expose egress mapping semantics), and `maintenance-fastlane` (playbook + CLI).

maya-field: Customers that raised this are in telecom and healthcare. Their procurement teams require: 1) cryptographic checksums and signed bundles, 2) a deterministic maintenance window, 3) proof that egress IPs won't change during the rollout. One customer offered a staging environment for testing.

trent-se: Draft config idea for network-handshake: ```network_handshake:
  enabled: true
  mode: pinned
  pinned_addresses:
    - "198.51.100.32/28"
  allow_reassign: false
  upgrade_policy: in_place_first
``` If allow_reassign=false, operator must attempt in-place patches and fail early if a change would reassign external mapping.

vik-engineering: Implementation notes: `in_place_first` tries non-disruptive workflows; if kernel-level changes require node replacement, the operator will abort and report `upgrade_blocked_by_kernel`. That needs to be documented so legal/field can set expectations.

sam-prod: How many customers will block on this? Maya?

maya-field: Two paying prospects and one pilot said it's a hard blocker without network-handshake or a documented escape hatch. The pilot is willing to run verification in sprint+2.

claire-legal: Important: any promise around "won't change IPs" needs explicit contract language and defined exceptions (cloud provider maintenance, customer-side NAT changes, required host kernel upgrades). Send me the exact abort codes and semantics and I'll draft a networking appendix.

vik-engineering: Proposal timeline: sprint+1 -> compact-bundle alpha (signed tarball, verifier tool, no outbound by default). sprint+2 -> network-handshake experimental (config + abort semantics + dry-run simulation). sprint+3 -> maintenance-fastlane docs + pilot validation for GA criteria.

sam-prod: Acceptance criteria for compact-bundle alpha: 1) installer runs fully offline using the bundled artifacts; 2) local verifier checks signatures and checksums; 3) telemetry disabled by default with an audit-only trace option.

trent-se: For the network-handshake dry-run we'll add `rwin upgrade --handshake --dry-run` which simulates the steps and emits metrics: `simulated_ip_drift_count`, `simulated_outage_secs`, `upgrade_blockers`. That gives field a safe way to validate.

maya-field: Pilot customer will run dry-run first and then a single-node canary. They also asked for a short preflight checklist: capture ip map, snapshot NAT configs, run dry-run with logs attached.

vik-engineering: We'll also add a `handshake_mode: advisory` option so customers can preview potential drifts without blocking the upgrade (helpful for early validation).

sam-prod: Good. Legal: Claire, you'll prepare appendix draft once we share abort semantics.

claire-legal: Yes. Also recommend adding a customer opt-in signature on the installer agreement for the handshake feature, noting it's beta until pilot completes.

bot-deploy: ticket created: PD-13001 (compact-bundle-alpha), PD-13002 (network-handshake-dry-run), PD-13003 (maintenance-fastlane-docs).

vik-engineering: Dev owners: I'll take compact-bundle + verifier. Trent will own network-handshake implementation + simulator. Acceptance tests: offline e2e, dry-run simulator assertions, and canary reversion test.

maya-field: I'll secure pilot and produce the preflight matrix. Targeting sprint+2 test window.

sam-prod: Decision summary: compact-bundle alpha sprint+1; network-handshake experimental + dry-run sprint+2; maintenance-fastlane & pilot validation sprint+3 for GA gating. Action items: vik -> PD-13001, trent -> PD-13002, maya -> pilot coordination, claire -> contract appendix. I'll update the roadmap doc and publish sprint cards. :thumbsup:
